response.sql:
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(CAST(rental_rate AS DOUBLE) / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio
  FROM film
  WHERE replacement_cost > 20.99
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean FROM per_rating
)
SELECT p.rating, p.avg_ratio, p.avg_ratio - o.overall_mean AS above_overall_mean
FROM per_rating p
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE o.overall_mean IS NOT NULL
  AND p.avg_ratio > o.overall_mean;

assumptions.assumption: Each distinct film.rating value is one group, and a NULL rating (if any existed) would form its own group; the verified data shows only the five MPAA ratings.
The division is done in double precision so the per-rating averages and the difference are unrounded, since MySQL decimal division would otherwise round to a fixed number of decimal places.
rental_duration is never zero (the verified profile shows values 3 to 7), so the division cannot fail; rental_rate and rental_duration are NOT NULL, so AVG ignores no rows within a group.
The 'simple mean of per-rating averages' is an unweighted AVG over the per-rating averages, not a film-weighted mean.
